title: Tina Takes Her Time
summary: Tina the tortoise wants to be as fast as the rabbit. She tries, ends up flat on her back, and from down there discovers something the rabbit has never seen.

scenes.text:
Tina was a very slow tortoise.

So slow that butterflies landed on her shell thinking she was a stone. So slow that once a snail overtook her, and waved goodbye as it went.

Tina didn't mind. She ambled across the meadow, looking at things, and she always got where she meant to go.

Until that morning.

She was crossing the path when something went past so close and so fast that it sent the leaves around her spinning.

It was the rabbit. He was already miles away, ears flat back, kicking up a cloud of dust.

All he left behind was the air still moving, and a long whistle.

Tina stared at the dust.

"I can do that too," she said.

And she started to run.

Well. To run the way a tortoise runs. She moved her legs as fast as she could, plomp, plomp, plomp, her shell wobbling from side to side.

After five steps she was out of breath.

She rested a moment and tried again, this time with her eyes shut, because that made her feel faster.

With her eyes shut, she didn't see the stone.

She tripped, turned right over in the air, and landed upside down, tummy up, all four legs pointing at the sky.

Thud.

Tina waved her legs. She waved her head. She rocked to one side and then the other.

There was no way to turn over.

At first she was very cross indeed. Then she got tired of being cross. And since there was nothing else to do, she lay still and looked up.

Up above there was a cloud shaped like a sock.

Next to it, another one shaped like a smaller sock, as if they were a pair.

A red ladybird climbed up one of her legs, very serious, as if it were on its way somewhere important. And along the edge of her shell marched a line of ants, each one carrying a scrap of green leaf.

Without noticing, Tina was smiling.

The rabbit came racing past again.

And braked. He skidded, sprayed up earth, and hopped back to look at her.

"Are you all right? You're upside down."

"I know," said Tina.

The rabbit nudged her with his nose, once, twice, and on the third go Tina rolled over and was the right way up again.

"So why were you smiling?" asked the rabbit. "You were upside down and smiling."

Tina showed him the sock-shaped clouds. The ladybird, still on its way. The ants with their scraps of leaf.

The rabbit stared with his mouth open.

"I come past here every single day," he said slowly. "And I've never seen any of this."

Ever since that day, the rabbit still runs his races across the meadow every morning, ears flat back.

But in the afternoons, he comes to find Tina.

And they walk together for a good long while. Her in front and him behind, learning to go slowly, which is the hardest thing in the world for a rabbit.

Tina shows him things. A stone shaped like a heart. A blue feather. A beetle as shiny as a button.

They are in no hurry at all. On the path, all you can hear is their footsteps.
